page_new.excerpt: # Retries and backpressure **Question.** When do retries absorb transient failure, and when do they amplify overload? **Short answer.** A retry helps only when the failure is transient and the retry budget is bounded. Without a budget, backoff and jitter, retries add load to an already saturated system. Backpressure, queue capacity and a bulkhead decide whether the system rejects work explicitly or collapses under it.
